places.name: Victoria Peak (The Peak)
places.notes: Iconic viewpoint over Victoria Harbour; reachable via Peak Tram, bus, or taxi.

places.name: Victoria Harbour
places.notes: Waterfront promenades on both sides of the harbour, including Central and Tsim Sha Tsui.

places.name: Avenue of Stars
places.notes: Promenade with statues and handprints dedicated to Hong Kong film stars.

places.name: Tian Tan Buddha (Big Buddha)
places.notes: Large outdoor seated bronze Buddha near Po Lin Monastery; reached via Ngong Ping cable car or bus.

places.name: Ngong Ping 360 Cable Car
places.address: Tung Chung and Ngong Ping terminals
places.notes: 5.7 km cable car connecting Tung Chung to Ngong Ping Village, passing over bay and hills.

places.name: Ocean Park Hong Kong
places.notes: Marine-themed park with rides, giant pandas, and cable car along southern coastline.

places.name: Hong Kong Disneyland
places.notes: Disney resort with themed lands and shows, accessible via MTR Disneyland Resort Line.

places.name: Temple Street Night Market
places.notes: Street market selling garments, jewellery and gadgets; near Tin Hau Temple with fortune tellers.

places.name: Stanley Market
places.notes: Souvenir and clothing market with waterfront restaurants and bars.

places.name: Man Mo Temple
places.notes: Historic temple dedicated to gods of literature and war; known for hanging incense coils.

places.name: Tai O Fishing Village
places.notes: Traditional village with stilt houses on Lantau's northwestern shore.

places.name: Aberdeen Fishing Village
places.notes: Fishing community with boat rides around the harbour to see traditional lifestyle.

places.name: Lan Kwai Fong
places.notes: Cluster of streets in Central known for dense bars and nightlife.

places.name: Dragon's Back Hike
places.notes: Popular ridge hike on eastern Hong Kong Island with coastal views.

places.name: Tai Mo Shan
places.notes: Highest peak in Hong Kong, with lush terrain and nearby traditional villages.

places.name: IFC Mall
places.notes: Large mall above Hong Kong Station with many international luxury brands.

places.name: Harbour City
places.notes: Largest mall in Hong Kong with ~700 shops and harbourfront location near Star Ferry.

places.name: Elements
places.notes: Large mall above Kowloon Station, divided into themed zones based on Chinese elements.

places.name: Langham Place
places.notes: Vertical mall with youth-focused brands and a long escalator; popular among young shoppers.

places.name: Times Square
places.notes: Major mall and office complex with fashion brands and frequent outdoor installations.

places.name: Pacific Place
places.notes: High-end mall connected to hotels and office towers, near Hong Kong Park.

places.name: New Town Plaza
places.address: 18 Sha Tin Centre Street, Sha Tin
places.notes: Large complex near Sha Tin MTR with numerous shops and dining options.

places.name: Festival Walk
places.notes: Mall above Kowloon Tong MTR with ice rink, cinema, and diverse retail.

places.name: MegaBox
places.notes: Large mall with big-box tenants including furniture and electronics stores.

places.name: Citygate Outlets
places.notes: Outlet mall near Tung Chung MTR with many discounted international brands.

places.name: SOGO Causeway Bay
places.notes: Large Japanese department store with many floors of fashion and lifestyle goods.

places.name: Olympian City
places.notes: Complex of malls near Olympic MTR station.

places.name: Telford Plaza
places.notes: Neighbourhood mall above Kowloon Bay MTR.

popular.name: Victoria Peak (The Peak)
popular.notes: Classic Hong Kong skyline view; frequently listed in top-attraction roundups.

popular.name: Victoria Harbour
popular.notes: Harbour & skyline category highlight on Hong Kong Tourism Board's Top Picks.

popular.name: Hong Kong Disneyland
popular.notes: Flagship theme park and one of the city's most visited attractions.

popular.name: Ocean Park Hong Kong
popular.area: Wong Chuk Hang, Hong Kong Island
popular.notes: Marine-themed park with rides and animal exhibits; long-time local favourite.

popular.name: Tian Tan Buddha (Big Buddha)
popular.notes: Giant seated Buddha above Ngong Ping Village; frequently in top things to do lists.

popular.name: Ngong Ping 360 Cable Car
popular.area: Tung Chung to Ngong Ping, Lantau Island
popular.notes: 24-minute cable car offering views of airport, sea and hills; gateway to Ngong Ping Village.

popular.name: Avenue of Stars
popular.notes: Film-themed promenade honouring Hong Kong cinema with statues and handprints.

popular.name: Star Ferry
popular.area: Central / Wan Chai to Tsim Sha Tsui
popular.notes: Green-and-white ferries crossing Victoria Harbour; part of the city's identity.

popular.name: Hong Kong Observation Wheel
popular.notes: Ferris wheel giving harbour and skyline views from Central's waterfront.

popular.name: West Kowloon Cultural District
popular.notes: Arts hub with M+ museum, Xiqu Centre and long waterfront promenade.

popular.name: Temple Street Night Market
popular.notes: Night market famous for street food, cheap goods and fortune tellers.

popular.name: Tai O Fishing Village
popular.notes: Traditional stilt-house village offering boat trips and seafood, often listed as a must-see day trip.

accessible.name: Accessible viewpoints at Victoria Peak (Findlay Path, Lugard Road, Peak Circle Walk)
accessible.notes: Localiiz highlights flat, wheelchair-friendly paths and lookouts on the Peak such as Lugard Road and the Peak Circle Walk.

accessible.name: Star Ferry (lower deck)
accessible.area: Central / Wan Chai to Tsim Sha Tsui
accessible.notes: Wheelchair Travel notes accessible lower deck boarding ramps, with variable steepness depending on pier and tides.

accessible.name: Ngong Ping 360 Cable Car
accessible.area: Tung Chung to Ngong Ping, Lantau Island
accessible.notes: Cable car has level-entry boarding and ample interior space, described as wheelchair accessible by Wheelchair Travel.

accessible.name: Nan Lian Garden
accessible.notes: Listed as one of the top wheelchair-accessible attractions, with barrier-free paths and traditional landscaping.

accessible.name: West Kowloon Cultural District Waterfront
accessible.notes: Localiiz recommends the district's flat waterfront and mentions a dedicated Accessibility Office offering guided tours.

accessible.name: Ma Wan Park - Tsing Ma Bridge Viewpoint
accessible.notes: Hilltop Lookout in Ma Wan Park accessed via barrier-free ramp, with views of Tsing Ma Bridge.

accessible.name: Tai Tam Reservoir Accessible Walk
accessible.notes: Localiiz describes a flat, accessible path from Tai Tam Country Park South Entrance to Tai Tam Tuk Masonry Bridge.

accessible.name: Hong Kong Disneyland (accessible facilities)
accessible.notes: Curb Free with Cory Lee notes adapted rides, accessible shuttle and paths designed for wheelchair users.

accessible.name: Avenue of Stars Promenade
accessible.notes: Described as flat and even, with easy access along the waterfront, suitable for wheelchairs.

accessible.name: Victoria Harbour Accessible Waterfronts
accessible.area: Central, Wan Chai, Tsim Sha Tsui
accessible.notes: Wheelchair Travel highlights accessible walks along the harbourfront and accessible lower deck of the Star Ferry.

hidden_gems.name: Tai Hang Neighbourhood
hidden_gems.notes: Agoda highlights Tai Hang for the Tai Hang Fire Dragon Dance and its small local restaurants and shops.

hidden_gems.name: Sham Shui Po Street Markets & Food
hidden_gems.notes: Listed as a hidden gem for traditional mooncake shops, electronics and fabric markets, and strong local street-food scene.

hidden_gems.name: Tsz Shan Monastery
hidden_gems.notes: Agoda describes this hill-side monastery with a giant Guan Yin statue and tranquil gardens as a serene hidden gem.

hidden_gems.name: Lai Chi Wo Hakka Village
hidden_gems.notes: Traditional Hakka village promoted as a hidden gem for sustainable agriculture and rural heritage.

hidden_gems.name: Kowloon Walled City Park
hidden_gems.notes: Park built on the site of the former densest urban enclave; now a landscaped garden with historical exhibits.

hidden_gems.name: Peng Chau Island
hidden_gems.notes: Agoda lists Peng Chau as a peaceful retreat with temples, small beaches and local snacks like pineapple buns.

hidden_gems.name: Sha Tau Kok Closed Town Area
hidden_gems.notes: Featured as a lesser-visited closed town offering insight into border-area history and culture when special access is allowed.

hidden_gems.name: Hidden Alleyway Cafés
hidden_gems.area: Various (Tai Hang, Sheung Wan, Sham Shui Po)
hidden_gems.notes: Article mentions tucked-away coffee shops as part of Hong Kong's hidden gems; treat this as a general category to be detailed later.

hidden_gems.name: Cat Street (Upper Lascar Row)
hidden_gems.area: Sheung Wan / Central, Hong Kong Island
hidden_gems.notes: Highlighted in the shopping guide section for unique antiques and curios, away from big malls.

hidden_gems.name: Temple Street Night Market (local side streets)
hidden_gems.notes: Beyond the main tourist strip, smaller lanes with food stalls and live music are described as more authentic local experiences.
